_comment: One colour per arm, keyed by the arm's `short` -- the same string that names it on the
command line, in a legend and in the path its figures are written to. A reader who has
learnt that the production engine is blue never has to relearn it.
Colour is the ONLY identity channel: every series is drawn with the same marker and a
solid line, so a figure carries one visual variable rather than three.
Eight hues, a validated categorical palette (light surface; colour-vision-deficiency and
normal-vision separation checked pairwise) -- never add a ninth, reuse one instead. Two
arms may share a hue only if they are never compared in one figure, and
scripts/figure_layout.py refuses to draw a figure where two arms collide.
The kit modes wear the same hues in the OpenFold3 kit and the AlphaFold 3 kit -- off violet,
exact yellow, fast aqua -- because those are never compared across kits: each is read against
the stock arm on its own card. `big` is the exception: the two kits' `big` arms ARE compared,
so the AlphaFold 3 one takes orange. It then shares orange with stock OpenFold3, which it is
never drawn beside; if that ever changes, figure_layout.py will refuse and one of them moves.
Hues: blue #2a78d6  orange #eb6834  aqua #1baf7a  yellow #eda100  magenta #e87ba4
`role` is documentation: nothing reads it, it says why a slot was chosen.

af3-ob.role: AF3 code, openbind weights, RTX PRO 6000 -- the production engine

of3kit-big-gated.role: the same with the card table's reach gate left in place

af3kit-big-a100.role: AlphaFold 3 kit, mode big -- orange, not the OpenFold3 kit's green: the two `big` arms ARE compared with each other

af3-native-tmpl.role: AF3 code and weights, templates on (benchmark only)

af3-ob-tmpl.role: AF3 code, openbind weights, templates on (benchmark only)

zheng.role: Zheng & Peng's own AlphaFold 3 predictions (benchmark only)
